paragraphs: Gulls are a big problem for some people in Dublin. In St Stephen's Green, the birds fly down and take food from people's hands. They take sandwiches, pizza and ice cream.
Last summer, many people wrote to the city councils about the birds. Some birds made nests on roofs and chimneys. They made a lot of noise and attacked people near their homes.

But bird experts say people are the real problem. The number of herring gulls in Ireland is down by about 90% in 30 years. These birds once found food behind fishing boats. Now boats throw nothing away. Many rubbish dumps also closed, so the hungry birds moved into towns.
The birds are protected by EU law. A city business group says people should be careful with food outside.
sentZh: 海鷗對都柏林的一些人來說是個大問題。
在聖史蒂芬綠地公園，這些鳥會飛下來從人們手中搶食物。
牠們會搶三明治、披薩和冰淇淋。
去年夏天，很多人寫信給市議會抱怨海鷗。
有些鳥在屋頂和煙囪上築巢。
牠們製造很多噪音，還在住家附近攻擊人。
但鳥類專家說，人類才是真正的問題。
愛爾蘭銀鷗的數量在30年內減少了約90%。
這些鳥以前在漁船後面找食物。
現在漁船什麼都不丟。
許多垃圾場也關閉了，所以飢餓的鳥兒搬進了城鎮。
這些鳥受到歐盟法律保護。
一個城市商業團體說，人們在戶外吃東西時要小心。

paragraphs: If you eat lunch outside in Dublin, you may need to watch the sky. In St Stephen's Green, gulls often dive down and grab sandwiches, pizza and ice cream from people's hands.

The problem is not new. Last summer, residents sent many complaints to Dublin City Council and Fingal County Council. Some said gulls built nests behind their chimneys and kept them awake for weeks. Others said the birds attacked children, dog walkers and even pets.
However, wildlife groups say humans are to blame. Niall Hatch of BirdWatch Ireland says the number of herring gulls has fallen by about 90% in just three decades. He calls them a species in crisis.

Biologist Éanna Ní Lamhna explains why the birds came to towns. In the past, gulls followed fishing boats and ate the fish that crews threw away. Modern boats waste nothing. When rubbish dumps closed, the gulls moved into towns to find food.
Gulls are protected under EU law. Gerry Farrell of the business group Dublin Town says people should simply be careful with their food in public places.
sentZh: 如果你在都柏林戶外吃午餐，可能得注意天空。
在聖史蒂芬綠地公園，海鷗常常俯衝下來，從人們手中搶走三明治、披薩和冰淇淋。
這個問題並不新鮮。
去年夏天，居民向都柏林市議會和芬戈郡議會提出許多投訴。
有些人說海鷗在他們的煙囪後面築巢，讓他們好幾個星期睡不著。
也有人說這些鳥攻擊兒童、遛狗的人，甚至寵物。
然而，野生動物團體說該怪的是人類。
愛爾蘭鳥類保育組織的尼爾．哈奇說，銀鷗的數量在短短三十年內減少了約90%。
他稱牠們為陷入危機的物種。
生物學家艾安娜．尼．拉夫納解釋了這些鳥為什麼來到城鎮。
過去，海鷗跟著漁船，吃船員丟掉的魚。
現代漁船什麼都不浪費。
垃圾場關閉後，海鷗就搬進城鎮找食物。

paragraphs: Eating lunch outdoors in Dublin can be risky. In St Stephen's Green, gulls regularly swoop down and snatch sandwiches, slices of pizza and ice creams straight from people's hands.

Freedom of information records show that aggressive gulls led to a large number of complaints to Dublin City and Fingal councils last summer. Residents described birds nesting behind chimneys, weeks of lost sleep, and gulls diving at children, dog walkers and pets.

Conservation groups, however, argue that people are the real problem. Niall Hatch of BirdWatch Ireland points out that the herring gull population has dropped by around 90 per cent in only three decades, and he describes the bird as a species in crisis. Gulls are protected under the EU Birds Directive.

According to biologist Éanna Ní Lamhna, the birds' traditional food sources have disappeared. Gulls once followed fishing boats, but modern trawlers freeze their catch and throw nothing overboard. When landfill sites closed, many gulls moved into towns in search of food.
Gerry Farrell of the business group Dublin Town says the problem has eased in recent years, but he advises people to take care with food in public spaces.
sentZh: 在都柏林戶外吃午餐可能有風險。
在聖史蒂芬綠地公園，海鷗經常俯衝而下，直接從人們手中搶走三明治、披薩片和冰淇淋。
資訊公開紀錄顯示，去年夏天具攻擊性的海鷗讓都柏林市議會和芬戈郡議會收到大量投訴。
居民描述了海鷗在煙囪後築巢、好幾週睡眠不足，以及海鷗俯衝攻擊兒童、遛狗者和寵物的情形。
然而，保育團體認為人類才是真正的問題。
愛爾蘭鳥類保育組織的尼爾．哈奇指出，銀鷗的數量在僅僅三十年內下降了約九成，他形容這是一個陷入危機的物種。
海鷗受到歐盟《鳥類指令》保護。
生物學家艾安娜．尼．拉夫納表示，這些鳥的傳統食物來源已經消失。
海鷗過去跟隨漁船覓食，但現代拖網漁船會把漁獲冷凍，什麼都不丟進海裡。
垃圾掩埋場關閉後，許多海鷗搬進城鎮尋找食物。
商業團體「都柏林鎮」的傑瑞．法瑞爾說，問題近年來已有所緩和，但他建議民眾在公共空間吃東西時要小心。

paragraphs: Lunching al fresco in Dublin is not without its hazards. In St Stephen's Green, gulls routinely swoop on unsuspecting diners, making off with sandwiches, pizza and ice cream in broad daylight.

Records released under freedom of information legislation reveal that Dublin City and Fingal councils were inundated with complaints about aggressive gulls last summer. Exasperated residents reported birds nesting behind chimneys, weeks of disrupted sleep, and gulls dive-bombing children, dog walkers and even pets.

Wildlife campaigners, however, insist that the blame lies squarely with humans. Niall Hatch of BirdWatch Ireland notes that the herring gull population has plummeted by roughly 90 per cent in a mere three decades, describing it as a species in crisis. The birds are protected under the EU Birds Directive.

Biologist Éanna Ní Lamhna attributes the shift to the loss of the gulls' traditional food supply. The birds once trailed fishing vessels, but today's freezer trawlers discard nothing overboard. Once landfill sites were shut down, the gulls migrated into towns to forage.
Gerry Farrell of the business group Dublin Town acknowledges that the nuisance has abated somewhat, yet he urges the public to remain vigilant with food in public spaces.

依據資訊公開法公布的紀錄顯示，去年夏天都柏林市議會與芬戈郡議會被大量關於兇猛海鷗的投訴淹沒。
不堪其擾的居民反映海鷗在煙囪後築巢、好幾週睡眠受擾，以及海鷗俯衝攻擊兒童、遛狗者甚至寵物。
然而，野生動物倡議人士堅稱，責任完全在於人類。
愛爾蘭鳥類保育組織的尼爾．哈奇指出，銀鷗數量在短短三十年間暴跌約九成，並形容牠們是陷入危機的物種。
這些鳥受到歐盟《鳥類指令》保護。
生物學家艾安娜．尼．拉夫納將這種轉變歸因於海鷗傳統食物來源的喪失。
這些鳥過去尾隨漁船，但如今的冷凍拖網漁船不會把任何東西丟棄到海裡。
垃圾掩埋場一關閉，海鷗便遷入城鎮覓食。
商業團體「都柏林鎮」的傑瑞．法瑞爾承認，這種滋擾已稍有減輕，但他敦促民眾在公共空間對食物保持警覺。

Documents obtained under freedom of information legislation indicate that Dublin City and Fingal councils received a substantial volume of complaints regarding aggressive gulls last summer. Residents cited birds nesting behind chimneys, prolonged sleep deprivation, and attacks on children, dog walkers and domestic animals.

Nevertheless, conservationists maintain that responsibility rests primarily with humans. Niall Hatch of BirdWatch Ireland observes that the herring gull population has declined by approximately 90 per cent within three decades, a trend he characterises as a crisis for the species. The biologist Éanna Ní Lamhna attributes this phenomenon to the depletion of the birds' traditional food sources. Gulls historically depended on fishing vessels, yet contemporary freezer trawlers discard no waste at sea. Following the closure of landfill sites, the birds relocated to urban areas in pursuit of sustenance.
Gerry Farrell of the business group Dublin Town concedes that the problem has diminished to some extent, although he recommends that the public exercise caution with food in shared spaces.
